light.notes: Bright, indirect light, such as an east-facing window. Direct midday sun burns the leaves.

water.notes: Water when the bark is nearly dry and the roots look silvery. Soak for 10 minutes, then drain completely. Never leave water sitting in the crown.
water.restingSeason: Every 10–14 days.

soil.notes: Coarse orchid bark in a pot with plenty of drainage — never ordinary compost.

guides.feeding: Orchid feed at quarter to half strength every 2 weeks — 'weakly, weekly' is the rule.
guides.repotting: Every 1–2 years after flowering, once the bark starts to break down.
guides.pruning: After flowering, cut the spike just above a node to encourage a side spike, or at the base to let it rest.
guides.propagation: Baby plants (keikis) sometimes form on the flower spike; pot them once they have roots 5cm long.

problems.fix: Give it a few weeks of nights around 15°C in autumn, with bright light by day.
Check the roots: trim any brown and mushy ones and repot in fresh bark.

problems.cause: Water left sitting in the centre
problems.fix: Tip out any water after watering. A rotted crown rarely recovers.

guides.growthHabit: Epiphyte with broad, flat leaves, aerial roots and long arching flower spikes.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light, such as an east or north window. Hot sun scorches the leaves.

water.notes: Water from below, or at the compost, with room-temperature water. Cold water on the leaves leaves pale spots.
water.growingSeason: When the surface feels dry — often weekly.
water.restingSeason: Slightly less.

guides.feeding: African violet feed at the label strength every 2 weeks while flowering.
guides.repotting: Every year into fresh mix, keeping the pot small.
guides.pruning: Pick off spent flowers and damaged outer leaves.
guides.propagation: Leaf cuttings with a short stalk, in water or compost.

problems.symptom: Pale rings or spots on leaves
problems.fix: Water from below with room-temperature water.
Move it somewhere brighter, out of direct sun.
Let it dry more; restart from a healthy leaf if the crown has rotted.

guides.growthHabit: Low rosette of fuzzy leaves with clusters of violet, pink or white flowers.

light.notes: A bright, cool spot out of direct sun.

water.notes: Water from below when the surface feels dry, keeping water off the tuber. It flowers in the cool months and rests in summer.
water.growingSeason: After flowering in spring the leaves yellow and it rests. Water very little until late summer.
water.restingSeason: Its flowering season: water from below whenever the surface is dry.

soil.notes: Free-draining compost, with the top of the tuber above the surface.

toxicity.notes: Contains saponins, concentrated in the tuber. Eating it causes drooling, vomiting and diarrhoea; heart rhythm problems are rare.

guides.feeding: Half-strength high-potash feed every 2 weeks while in flower.
guides.repotting: In late summer, as new leaves appear.
guides.pruning: Twist off spent flowers and yellow leaves right down at the tuber.

problems.symptom: Leaves yellowing and collapsing in winter
problems.fix: Keep it in a cool room (10–18°C) and water from below.

problems.symptom: Grey, fuzzy mould at the base
problems.fix: Remove affected parts and water only from below.

problems.symptom: All leaves dying back in spring
problems.fix: Normal. Keep it almost dry until new leaves appear in late summer.

guides.growthHabit: Heart-shaped, silver-marbled leaves and swept-back flowers from a tuber.

light.notes: Bright light with gentle morning sun; indoors, a bright and fairly cool spot.

water.notes: Keep evenly moist with rainwater or lime-free water. It hates lime.
water.growingSeason: Water as the surface starts to dry.
water.restingSeason: Slightly less, never letting it dry out.

toxicity.notes: Listed as toxic to cats and dogs. Eating it can cause mild vomiting, diarrhoea and hives.

guides.feeding: Ericaceous feed every 2 weeks in spring and summer.
guides.repotting: Every 2–3 years in spring, into ericaceous compost.
guides.propagation: Softwood cuttings in spring, with warmth.

problems.cause: Dry air, temperature swings, being moved, or dry compost
problems.fix: Keep it in one bright spot at a steady temperature, and keep the compost moist.

problems.cause: Lime in the water or soil locking out iron
problems.fix: Water with rainwater and use an ericaceous feed with iron.

problems.symptom: Sticky leaves or black sooty patches
problems.fix: Wipe them off and check the undersides of leaves weekly.

guides.growthHabit: Evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and intensely scented white flowers.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light.

water.notes: Keep a little water in the central cup, refreshing it weekly, and keep the compost just moist. Use rainwater or filtered water if you can.
water.restingSeason: Keep the cup only a quarter full in cool rooms.

soil.notes: Very free-draining bark mix; its roots mainly anchor it.

guides.feeding: A weak liquid feed into the cup monthly in summer.
guides.repotting: Rarely needed; pot up offsets instead.
guides.propagation: Each rosette flowers once, then slowly dies while producing pups. Separate them once a third the size of the parent.

problems.fix: Let it fade while the pups grow, then cut it away.
Flush the cup with fresh water regularly and keep it warm.

guides.growthHabit: Rosette of glossy strap leaves with a long-lasting red, orange or yellow flower head.

light.notes: Bright light with a little gentle sun keeps the silver banding strong.

water.notes: Keep the central urn topped up with fresh water, emptying and refilling it every week or two. Keep the compost barely moist.
water.restingSeason: Keep it only partly filled in cool rooms.

guides.feeding: A weak feed into the urn monthly in summer.

problems.fix: Grow on the offsets.
Use rainwater and raise the humidity.

guides.growthHabit: Vase-shaped rosette of silver-banded leaves with a pink flower head.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light. Dark corners starve it.

water.notes: Soak it in rainwater or filtered water for 20–30 minutes, then shake off the water and dry it upside down. It must be completely dry within 4 hours or it rots.
water.restingSeason: Soak every 2 weeks.

soil.notes: No soil at all: rest it in a dish, or mount it on wood. Never plant it in compost.

guides.feeding: Bromeliad or air plant feed in the soaking water once a month.
guides.propagation: Pups form around the base after flowering; separate when a third of the parent's size.

problems.symptom: Brown, mushy base; leaves falling out of the centre
problems.fix: Always dry it upside down after soaking, with good airflow.
Soak for longer or more often.

guides.growthHabit: Small, silvery rosette that blushes red before flowering.

light.notes: Full sun to flower well; outdoors only in warm summers.

water.notes: Keep lightly moist through summer — it's thirsty while flowering.
water.growingSeason: Often every 2–3 days in warm weather.
water.restingSeason: Every 1–2 weeks, letting the top dry.

guides.pruning: Cut back by up to a third in early spring; flowers form on new growth.
guides.propagation: Softwood cuttings in spring or summer.

problems.cause: Dry compost, a move, or cold
problems.fix: Water consistently and keep it in one warm, bright place.
Check the compost and keep it above 10°C.
Squash them or rinse them off with water.

guides.growthHabit: Evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and large, short-lived flowers.

light.notes: Full sun outdoors; a bright windowsill indoors.

water.notes: Keep the compost moist. Potted mums wilt quickly when dry.
water.growingSeason: Check pots daily in warm weather.
water.restingSeason: Keep garden plants on the dry side over winter.

toxicity.notes: Contains pyrethrins and other irritants. Eating it causes vomiting, diarrhoea and drooling; handling can irritate skin.

guides.feeding: Balanced feed every 2 weeks until buds show colour.
guides.repotting: Pot mums are often grown as seasonal plants; garden types can be divided in spring.
guides.pruning: Pinch the tips until early summer for bushy plants; cut back after flowering.

problems.fix: Water thoroughly and check pots often.
Improve airflow and water at the base.
Rinse or squash them.

guides.growthHabit: Bushy perennial with masses of daisy-like or pompom flowers in autumn.

light.notes: Full sun: a south-facing window, or outdoors in summer.

water.notes: Stand the pot in a tray of rainwater, distilled or reverse-osmosis water. The minerals in tap water slowly kill it.
water.growingSeason: Keep 1–2cm of rainwater in the tray.
water.restingSeason: It needs a cold winter rest (0–10°C) for about three months. Keep it just damp, not standing in water.

soil.notes: Carnivorous plant mix, or sphagnum moss with perlite. No compost and no fertiliser.

guides.feeding: Never fertilise. It catches its own insects. Don't trigger the traps for fun — each can only close a few times.
guides.repotting: Every 1–2 years in spring, into fresh carnivorous mix.
guides.pruning: Snip off blackened traps. Remove flower stalks early if you want stronger traps.
guides.propagation: Division of the rhizome in spring.

problems.cause: Normal after a trap has closed a few times — or tap water, or too little light
problems.fix: Trim dead traps, use only rainwater and give it full sun.

problems.symptom: Weak, floppy leaves with small traps
problems.fix: Move it into direct sun.
Give it a cold, bright rest over winter.

guides.growthHabit: Low rosette of hinged, toothed traps.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light, away from draughts and radiators.

water.notes: Water when the surface feels dry and never leave it standing in water.
water.restingSeason: When dry — often weekly in a warm room while in colour.

toxicity.notes: Listed as toxic to cats and dogs, though its reputation is worse than the reality: the milky sap causes mild mouth irritation, drooling and sometimes vomiting.

guides.feeding: Balanced feed monthly from spring to autumn if keeping it.
guides.repotting: In late spring, if keeping it for another year.
guides.pruning: Cut back to about 15cm in spring, wearing gloves.

problems.cause: A cold draught — even on the way home from the shop — or wet compost
problems.fix: Keep it warm and out of draughts, and let the surface dry between waterings.
Water thoroughly.

problems.symptom: Bracts stay green the next year
problems.fix: From October, give it 14 hours of total darkness each night for about eight weeks.

guides.growthHabit: Shrub whose red, pink or cream 'flowers' are really coloured leaves (bracts).

light.notes: Bright, indirect light; no midday sun.

water.notes: Soak when the bark is nearly dry and roots look silvery, then drain completely. Keep water out of the crown.
water.restingSeason: Every 10–14 days.

problems.fix: A few weeks of 15°C nights in autumn.
Trim mushy roots and repot in fresh bark.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Epiphytic orchids with broad leaves and arching spikes.

light.notes: More light than moth orchids, including some gentle sun.

water.notes: Water when the bark is nearly dry. Many types need a drier, cooler rest in winter to flower.
water.restingSeason: Much less for most types.

soil.notes: Coarse bark in a small pot.

genusFallbacks.feeding: Weak orchid feed every 2 weeks in growth.
genusFallbacks.repotting: Every 2 years; they like tight pots.
genusFallbacks.propagation: Keikis on the canes, or division.

problems.fix: Give it cooler nights and less water in winter.
Let the bark dry more.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Upright canes with flowers along or at the top.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light.

water.notes: Water at the compost or from below with room-temperature water; let the surface dry between waterings.
water.restingSeason: Slightly less.

genusFallbacks.feeding: Flowering-plant feed every 2 weeks while in bloom.

problems.fix: Water from below.
Let the surface dry first.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Rosettes of soft leaves with trumpet- or violet-shaped flowers.

light.notes: Florist's cyclamen want a bright, cool room; hardy garden cyclamen grow in shade under trees.

water.notes: Water around the tuber, never onto it. Most rest dry in summer.
water.restingSeason: Water when the surface is dry while in leaf.

toxicity.notes: Cyclamen contain saponins, especially in the tuber. Eating them causes drooling, vomiting and diarrhoea.

problems.fix: A cool room below 18°C.
Water from below.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Marbled leaves and swept-back flowers from a tuber.

light.notes: Your brightest window. Turn the pot so the stem grows straight.

water.notes: Water sparingly until the flower stalk appears, then keep it lightly moist. Keep water off the top of the bulb.
water.growingSeason: Keep the leaves growing after flowering to feed next year's bulb.
water.restingSeason: Many are rested dry and cool for 8–10 weeks from early autumn, then brought back into warmth to flower.

soil.notes: Free-draining compost, with the top third of the bulb above the surface.

toxicity.notes: Contains lycorine and other alkaloids, concentrated in the bulb. Eating it causes vomiting, diarrhoea, drooling and abdominal pain; tremors are possible.

genusFallbacks.feeding: Balanced feed every 2 weeks from flowering until the leaves yellow.
genusFallbacks.repotting: Every 2–3 years, in a pot just wider than the bulb.
genusFallbacks.pruning: Cut the flower stalk near the bulb once it fades; leave the leaves.

problems.cause: The bulb wasn't fed or rested
problems.fix: Feed the leaves all summer, then give it a dry, cool rest.
Water only once growth appears.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Large bulb with strap leaves and a tall stalk of trumpet flowers.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light.

water.notes: A little fresh water in the central cup, refreshed weekly; compost just moist.
water.restingSeason: Less in cool rooms.

problems.fix: Grow on the pups.
Refresh the cup.

light.notes: Bright light, with some gentle sun, for the best colour.

water.notes: Keep fresh water in the central cup and the mix barely moist.
water.restingSeason: Partly fill the cup in cool rooms.

problems.fix: More light.
Grow on the pups.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Flat rosettes whose centres blush red at flowering.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light.

water.notes: Soak in rainwater for 20–30 minutes, shake off and dry upside down within 4 hours. Silvery, fuzzy kinds need less water than smooth green ones.
water.restingSeason: Every 2 weeks.

soil.notes: No soil; mount it or rest it in a dish.

genusFallbacks.feeding: Air plant feed in the soaking water monthly.

problems.fix: Dry upside down with good airflow.
Soak more often.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Rootless rosettes that absorb water through their leaves.

light.notes: Full sun.

water.notes: Keep the soil moist.
water.restingSeason: Keep drier over winter.

toxicity.notes: Chrysanthemums contain pyrethrins and other irritants that cause vomiting, diarrhoea and drooling if eaten.

problems.fix: Water thoroughly.
Water at the base; space plants.

light.notes: Bright, indirect light; a little morning sun helps pitchers colour.

water.notes: Keep the mix moist with rainwater, distilled or reverse-osmosis water only — never tap water.
water.growingSeason: Water as the surface starts to dry.
water.restingSeason: Slightly less.

soil.notes: Sphagnum moss, bark and perlite. No compost and no fertiliser in the mix.

genusFallbacks.feeding: None needed; the pitchers catch insects.
genusFallbacks.pruning: Cut long vines back to encourage new pitchers.

problems.fix: Raise the humidity and give it more light.

problems.cause: Tap water or old pitchers dying back
problems.fix: Use rainwater; old pitchers dying off is normal.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Climbing vines with hanging pitchers at the leaf tips.

light.notes: Full sun, ideally outdoors.

water.notes: Stand in a tray of rainwater all summer; never use tap water.
water.restingSeason: Needs a cold winter rest; keep just damp.

genusFallbacks.feeding: None; it catches its own insects.
genusFallbacks.pruning: Cut off dead pitchers in early spring.

problems.fix: Full sun outdoors.

problems.cause: Tap water or no winter rest
problems.fix: Rainwater only and a cold winter.

genusFallbacks.growthHabit: Upright, trumpet-shaped pitchers from a rhizome.
